notes: All 18 assigned files (4,993 lines) fully read in <=300-line chunks (most in one chunk, since the largest is 375 lines) and hash-verified both before and after review against the CX01C_PARTITION.json inventory: zero drift, sha256_before == sha256_inventory == sha256_after for every file. protocol.ts was independently cross-checked byte-offset-for-byte-offset against server/protocol.hpp (FrameHeader layout, wire:: encode/decode, SeqTracker) and against all 8 vectors in server/tests/vectors/frames.txt via a standalone Python struct decode (no Node/tsc/JS tooling used anywhere in this review, per the audit rules) -- exact match, no conformance mismatch found. desktop/ survivals were checked by Grep only (candles.hpp, chart_widget.hpp, depth_ladder.hpp, quant_pages.hpp) per instructions, never read in full: half-open candle bucketing and float32 domain-rebasing both independently survived into live desktop/ code correctly; the client's crossed-book 'always refuse' model did NOT survive and should not, since desktop/depth_ladder.hpp documents a deliberate, different, live decision (P2-08) that a crossed book is legitimate and must render during the pre-open auction; footprint/aggressor-inference and the strategy payoff end-slope bound logic were grepped for and not found ported into desktop/ at all. Two findings filed, both P3/retired: C20-001 (ladderRows does not itself refuse a crossed snapshot -- confirmed exploitable-in-principle by the fact that even client/tests/ladder.test.ts itself always calls ladderRows directly, bypassing fromFrame) and C20-002 (EndSlopes.downside is computed, documented, and returned, but is never read by any bound decision or asserted by any test -- current behavior is verified correct, this is a dead/misleading-field hygiene risk for a future editor, not a wrong number today).
